articles.title: Study protocol: outcomes of REvision surgery after primary JOINt replacement (REJOIN) study : a prospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Rijntjes D, van der Wal RJP, Verdegaal SHM, Gosens T, van Oldenrijk J, de Windt TS, et al.
articles.population: Patients scheduled for revision hip or knee replacement surgery and their significant others
articles.outcomes: Patient expectations and their fulfilment, mental wellbeing, pain, function, quality of life, caregiver burden, and health outcomes for significant others measured using validated questionnaires at baseline and up to 24 months
articles.take_home: This study will examine how revision joint replacement surgery affects patients' pain, function and mental wellbeing, as well as the burden experienced by their family members and carers. The results will help understand what patients hope for after revision surgery and whether those hopes are met.

articles.title: Retatrutide Once Weekly in Adults with Knee Osteoarthritis Pain and Obesity.
articles.authors: Schnitzer TJ, Hunter DJ, Conaghan PG, Sharma AM, Pedersen SD, Chen K, et al.
articles.population: Adults without diabetes, painful knee osteoarthritis, body mass index at least 27
articles.outcomes: Change in knee pain (WOMAC pain score, range 0-10) and body weight percentage change at 68-80 weeks
articles.take_home: Retatrutide, given as a weekly injection, reduced knee pain more than placebo and also led to substantial weight loss (20-24% with retatrutide versus 4-5% with placebo) in people with osteoarthritis and obesity. However, retatrutide caused more side effects than placebo, mainly stomach and bowel problems.

articles.title: Patellofemoral joint cartilage status was not deteriorated after inverted V-shaped high tibial osteotomy.
articles.authors: Hayashi S, Kato K
articles.population: Adults with medial compartment osteoarthritis of the knee
articles.outcomes: Patellofemoral joint alignment and cartilage status measured by imaging and arthroscopy; patient-reported outcomes including pain, function, and anterior knee pain
articles.take_home: Inverted V-shaped high tibial osteotomy successfully corrected knee alignment in patients with medial compartment osteoarthritis without damaging the patellofemoral joint cartilage. All patients reported improved function and relief from anterior knee pain.

articles.title: Beyond Traditional Approaches: The Rush Rod Construct for Managing Chronic Periprosthetic Joint Infection in Total Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Apt E, Entezari B, Bua N, Ruangsomboon P, Tomescu S, Gollish J, et al.
articles.population: Patients with chronic periprosthetic joint infection following total knee arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 40 patients with mean age 66 years and median follow-up 39 months
articles.outcomes: Re-infection-free survival, Musculoskeletal Infection Society outcome reporting tool scores, knee range of motion, and construct-related complications
articles.take_home: The Rush Rod construct successfully prevented re-infection in 80% of patients and preserved good knee flexibility, either as a temporary spacer before final replacement or as a lasting solution in 23% of cases. This offers patients a reliable alternative to traditional spacer approaches for managing persistent knee infections after joint replacement.

articles.title: Comparison of Subvastus versus Medial Parapatellar Approach for Total Knee Arthroplasty: A GRADE Assessed Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Muneeb M, Ahmad A, Haq IU, Abbas MS, Bibi H, Naseem A, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Early postoperative pain, hospital stay length, time to straight leg raise, intraoperative blood loss, operative time, range of motion, and functional outcomes at one month to one year
articles.take_home: The subvastus approach may help patients go home slightly sooner (about three-quarters of a day earlier) and regain the ability to straighten their leg earlier than the medial parapatellar approach. However, there are no clear differences in pain relief or longer-term movement and function between the two surgical approaches.

articles.title: Opportunistic Computed Tomography-Derived Psoas Muscle Attenuation is Independently Associated With Achievement of Substantial Clinical Benefit After Total Hip Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Okamoto Y, Wakama H, Saika T, Tani K, Otsuki S
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty for hip osteoarthritis
articles.outcomes: Achievement of substantial clinical benefit at 24 months, defined as a 22-point or greater improvement in Hip Disability and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score for Joint Replacement
articles.take_home: Patients with higher psoas muscle density on preoperative CT scans were more likely to achieve significant improvement in hip function after hip replacement surgery. Muscle density correlated with frailty and nutritional status, suggesting it may reflect overall health.

articles.title: Concurrent Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitor and Factor Xa Inhibitor Use Is Associated With Increased Transfusion and Periprosthetic Joint Infection After Primary Total Hip Arthroplasty Despite Tranexamic Acid.
articles.authors: Rice SW, Mehta S, Hall RR 3rd, Proffitt EB, Ayers DC
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study with propensity-score matching
articles.population: Adult patients undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty who received tranexamic acid
articles.outcomes: Allogeneic red blood cell transfusion (primary); surgical site infection, venous thromboembolism, periprosthetic joint infection, and revision hip replacement at 30, 90, and 365 days (secondary)
articles.take_home: Patients taking SSRIs before hip replacement had higher transfusion and infection rates even with blood-loss prevention medication. Taking SSRIs together with blood thinners increased these risks further compared with blood thinners alone, but not compared with SSRIs alone.

articles.title: Pericapsular Nerve Group Block Significantly Reduces Morphine Consumption and Improves Early Recovery Following Primary Total Hip Arthroplasty: A Randomized Double-Blind Sham-Controlled Trial.
articles.authors: Demirkiran F, Ozdemir Kol I, Altun O
articles.population: Patients undergoing elective primary total hip arthroplasty under general anaesthesia
articles.outcomes: Morphine consumption at 24 hours, pain scores, time to first rescue analgesia, patient satisfaction, opioid-related adverse events
articles.take_home: Patients who received a pericapsular nerve group block before hip replacement surgery used about 79% less morphine after the operation and had less pain compared to those who did not receive the block. The block also reduced nausea and improved patient satisfaction without causing any complications.

articles.title: Height, Bone Quality, and Osteoarthritis Severity Predict Posterior Cruciate Ligament Footprint Injury Despite Using Robotic-Assisted Technology in Total Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Leggieri F, Wood JA, Sergis N, Wernecke GC, Chen DB, MacDessi SJ
articles.population: Patients undergoing robotic-assisted cruciate-retaining total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Posterior cruciate ligament footprint injury at time of prosthetic implantation; independent predictors identified through multivariate logistic regression
articles.take_home: Despite using robotic-assisted technology, about one in ten patients experienced injury to the posterior cruciate ligament footprint during knee replacement surgery. Patients who were shorter, had poor bone quality, or had more severe osteoarthritis were at higher risk of this injury.

articles.title: Patient-Reported Outcomes, Satisfaction, and Expectation Recalibration After Re-Revision Total Hip Arthroplasty: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Li L, She Z, Wang Z, Bian T, Zheng H, Yang D, et al.
articles.population: Patients who underwent re-revision total hip arthroplasty (second or subsequent revision on the same hip)
articles.sample_size: 80 patients with minimum two years follow-up (median 5.0 years)
articles.outcomes: Patient satisfaction (90% satisfied), Hip disability and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score for Joint Replacement improved from 33.9 to 90.9, EuroQol Visual Analog Scale improved from 50.0 to 90.0, anxiety and depression scores improved significantly
articles.take_home: Most patients (90%) were satisfied after re-revision hip replacement, with major improvements in pain, function and quality of life at five years follow-up. Patients had lower expectations before re-revision surgery than before their first revision, and those with higher anxiety or depression before surgery were less likely to be satisfied afterwards.

articles.title: Metaphyseal Sleeves for Bone Defects in Revision Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Sun M, Yan L, Chen H, Wei X, Han X, Wang Y
articles.population: Patients undergoing revision total knee replacement with metaphyseal sleeves for bone defects
articles.outcomes: Knee Society Score, knee flexion range, re-revision rate, aseptic loosening rate, osseointegration rate, periprosthetic joint infection rate
articles.take_home: Metaphyseal sleeves used in revision knee replacement show good results with high rates of bone integration and low rates of loosening. The main reason for failure was infection rather than the sleeve itself failing.

articles.title: Comparative Effectiveness of Contemporary Alignment Strategies in Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Tan GHC, Lim HA, Thorpe LR, Kon Kam King C, Moo IH
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 61 studies (22 randomised controlled trials, 39 observational studies) involving 7,822 patients
articles.outcomes: Primary outcome: Forgotten Joint Score. Secondary outcomes: Oxford Knee Score, Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index, range of motion and flexion
articles.take_home: Patient-specific alignment strategies such as functional alignment and unrestricted kinematic alignment showed small statistical improvements in the Forgotten Joint Score compared with standard mechanical alignment, but the clinical significance of these improvements is unclear. The evidence quality is low, and larger, better-designed studies are needed to determine whether these newer approaches are genuinely better for patients.

articles.title: Higher Patient Complexity Generates Greater Hospital Revenue Without Proportional Surgeon Compensation in Revision Total Joint Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Persaud SG, Ortiz S, Zepeda KE, Burgio C, Vigdorchik JM, Debbi EM
articles.study_type: Retrospective analysis of Medicare reimbursement data
articles.population: Patients undergoing revision total hip or knee arthroplasty (TJA)
articles.sample_size: 8,718 revision TJA procedures from 526 surgeons; 25,188 inpatient discharges from 1,083 hospitals in 2023
articles.outcomes: Hospital and surgeon reimbursement rates stratified by patient complexity (high-risk versus standard-risk based on comorbidity scores)
articles.take_home: When revision joint replacement patients are more medically complex, hospitals receive significantly more money from Medicare but surgeons do not receive proportionally higher payment. The payment gap between hospitals and surgeons widens for more complex patients, which may not fairly reflect the greater clinical burden surgeons manage.

articles.title: A Single Preemptive Dose of Intravenous Nefopam Augmenting Multimodal Analgesia for Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Prospective, Triple-Blind, Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.authors: Sukha K, Khasemsiri R, Sutthapakti B, Wanitcharoenporn W, Inta-Ngam T, Laoruengthana A
articles.population: Patients undergoing total knee replacement surgery
articles.outcomes: Pain scores at 24 hours, morphine use over 48 hours, nausea and vomiting, time to first walking, time to hospital discharge, heart rate changes
articles.take_home: A single dose of the painkiller nefopam given before knee replacement surgery reduced pain and the need for morphine after the operation, whilst helping patients go home about 8 hours earlier. The main side effect was a temporary increase in heart rate, which did not affect recovery.

articles.title: Public Perceptions of Minimally Invasive Total Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Fox BQ, Bolognesi MP, Seyler T, Wellman S, Ryan SP
articles.population: US adults aged 40 to 77 years
articles.outcomes: Public perceptions and expectations regarding soft-tissue disruption, incision size, postoperative pain, and functional recovery following minimally invasive versus traditional total knee replacement
articles.take_home: Most patients surveyed expected minimally invasive knee replacement to cause less tissue damage, involve smaller cuts, and result in faster recovery and less pain than traditional surgery. However, research shows that mid-term outcomes are actually similar between the two approaches, suggesting patients may have unrealistic expectations based on marketing claims.

articles.title: Economic Evaluation of Dual Mobility Versus Conventional Liners in High-Risk Primary Total Hip Arthroplasty in a Single-Payer Universal Healthcare System.
articles.authors: Koucheki R, Abbaspour R, Abbas A, Lex JR, Tomescu S, Pincus D, et al.
articles.study_type: Economic evaluation using Markov cohort model
articles.population: Patients at high risk of hip dislocation undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty (those with prior lumbar fusion, spino-pelvic imbalance, or neuromuscular disease)
articles.sample_size: Hypothetical cohort of 1,000 patients modelled over 10 years
articles.outcomes: Number of dislocations and revisions prevented, quality-adjusted life-years, incremental cost-effectiveness ratio, net monetary benefit
articles.take_home: Dual mobility hip liners prevent more dislocations and revisions than standard liners in high-risk patients and cost less money within two years, making them a cost-effective choice for the NHS. The study suggests dual mobility liners should be used first-line in high-risk patients rather than only after problems develop.

articles.title: Complications After Primary Total Joint Arthroplasty in Solid Organ Transplant Recipients.
articles.authors: Rosenberg SI, Chang THW, Jandzinski M, Wang Z, Hardy L, Kheir MM
articles.population: Solid organ transplant recipients undergoing primary total joint arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 103 joint replacements (69 hip, 34 knee) in 89 patients
articles.outcomes: Medical and surgical complication rates, periprosthetic joint infection rates, mortality, five-year survivorship
articles.take_home: Solid organ transplant recipients can safely have hip or knee replacement surgery with low rates of joint infection (around 3-4% at five years) when managed with coordinated multidisciplinary care. However, overall complication rates were higher than in the general population, and kidney transplant recipients appeared more at risk of developing joint infections.

articles.title: Diversity at Accredited US Medical Schools, Orthopaedic Surgery Residency Programs, and Arthroplasty Fellowships by Sex, Race, and Ethnicity.
articles.authors: Silvestre J, Sheth N, Chen AF, Peters CL, Lieberman JR, Nelson CL
articles.population: US medical students, orthopaedic surgery residents, and arthroplasty fellows at accredited training programmes
articles.outcomes: Representation of demographic groups (by sex, race, and ethnicity) at different stages of medical training and fellowship, measured as participation-to-prevalence ratios compared to US population
articles.take_home: Women, Black, Hispanic, and Native American trainees are significantly underrepresented in arthroplasty fellowships compared to medical school and the general US population, whilst men and Asian trainees are overrepresented. The research suggests recruitment efforts could be improved at earlier stages of medical training to increase diversity in orthopaedic arthroplasty.

articles.title: Constitutional Restoration versus Mechanical Neutral in the Younger Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Pre-Specified Bayesian Competing-Risk Analysis of Alignment Accuracy and Aseptic Revision.
articles.authors: Hoskins W, Gusho C, Rosser K, Lim M, Dunstall K
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort analysis with Bayesian competing-risk model
articles.population: Total knee arthroplasty patients younger than 65 years with pre- and postoperative long-leg radiographs and minimum two-year follow-up
articles.sample_size: 470 total knee arthroplasties in 376 patients with 26 aseptic revisions
articles.outcomes: Aseptic revision as primary endpoint; death and infection as competing events; Oxford Knee Score at six months as secondary outcome
articles.take_home: Deviating from mechanical neutral alignment was probably linked to higher revision rates in younger knee replacement patients, whilst personalising alignment to restore the patient's original alignment did not increase revision risk. The accuracy of achieving the intended alignment target matters more than which alignment philosophy is chosen.

articles.title: Referral Geography, Case Complexity, and Definitive Surgical Strategy in a Regional Specialized Center for Periprosthetic Joint Infection in China.
articles.authors: Mu W, Hu Q, Xu B, Guo W, Li Y, Li G, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing surgical treatment for periprosthetic joint infection of the hip or knee at a regional specialized referral centre in China
articles.sample_size: 492 consecutive patients between January 2017 and December 2024
articles.outcomes: Accumulated prereferral burden (symptom duration, sinus tract presence, prior procedures), type of definitive surgical strategy (single-stage revision versus debridement, antibiotics, and implant retention), infection-related failure
articles.take_home: Patients referred from further away had longer delays before treatment and more complex infections, and were more likely to need single-stage revision surgery rather than simpler procedures, but infection control outcomes were similar regardless of referral distance. The study suggests that specialised centres handle more complex cases from distant regions without worse results.

articles.title: Microenvironment of Bone and Joint Infection: Examining the Microenvironment.
articles.authors: Abbaszadeh A, Damirchi MH, Soleimani M, Ortega-Yago A, Javad Mortazavi SM, Citak M, et al.
articles.population: Patients with periprosthetic joint infection
articles.outcomes: Diagnostic accuracy of microenvironment biomarkers including extracellular vesicles, cell-free nucleic acids, and sequencing-based pathogen detection compared to conventional methods
articles.take_home: New molecular tests that examine the infected joint microenvironment show promise for diagnosing joint infections around artificial joints, particularly when bacteria hide in biofilms or cannot be cultured. However, these tests are not yet widely available in routine clinical practice because they need standardisation, further testing, and cost reduction.

articles.title: Postoperative Skeletal Muscle Relaxants and Risk of Periprosthetic Fracture After Total Hip Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Wertz S, Sells P, Shen V, Durbin J, Cui E, Winthrop I, et al.
articles.study_type: Observational cohort study using national database
articles.population: Adult patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty for femoral head or neck fracture or osteoarthritis between 2011 and 2025
articles.outcomes: 30-day odds of periprosthetic fracture and reoperation
articles.take_home: Patients given muscle relaxants after hip replacement surgery had higher chances of fracture near the implant within 30 days compared to those who did not receive these medications. The risk was especially high in patients with osteoarthritis who had not previously taken muscle relaxants.

articles.title: Perioperative Duloxetine for Persistent Postoperative Pain After Total Hip Arthroplasty: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.authors: Nishi M, Yoshikawa Y, Usui Y, Inoue E, Nakamura S, Nishida H, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty for osteoarthritis
articles.outcomes: Primary: daily average hip pain at three months using numerical rating scale. Secondary: functional outcomes using JHEQ and DAP scores, postoperative analgesic consumption, chronic postsurgical pain incidence
articles.take_home: Duloxetine taken for 12 weeks around the time of hip replacement did not reduce pain or prevent chronic pain at three months compared to standard care alone. However, patients taking duloxetine had better movement and mobility outcomes and needed fewer painkillers, though one in five patients stopped the medication due to side effects.

articles.title: Clinical predictors of lateral meniscal hypermobility and development of the Hypermobile Lateral Meniscus Syndrome Score.
articles.authors: Endara Urresta F, Barros Castro A, Penaherrera-Carrillo C
articles.population: Patients undergoing knee arthroscopy: 156 with lateral meniscal hypermobility, 171 with structural lateral meniscal tears without hypermobility, and 155 arthroscopic controls
articles.outcomes: Independent predictors of lateral meniscal hypermobility identified: intermittent locking, hyperflexion pain, rotational instability sensation, posterolateral pain, and popliteomeniscal fascicle abnormality on MRI. Hypermobile Lateral Meniscus Syndrome Score (HLMSS) developed with area under the curve of 0.91 (sensitivity 86.5%, specificity 84.8% at score >/=7)
articles.take_home: Researchers developed a scoring system to help identify patients with a specific type of knee problem where the meniscus moves excessively, using clinical symptoms and MRI findings. The score performed well at distinguishing patients with this condition from those without it, though further testing in routine clinical practice is needed before widespread use.

articles.title: Meniscus extrusion assessed by ultrasound does not correlate with knee function or radiographic signs of joint degeneration after medial and lateral meniscus allograft transplantation at a mean follow-up of 13 years.
articles.authors: Wackerle AM, Park YL, Inoue J, Vieider RP, Kamada K, Herman ZJ, et al.
articles.population: Patients who underwent medial or lateral meniscus allograft transplantation with minimum 5-year follow-up
articles.outcomes: Meniscus extrusion measured by ultrasound, knee function (IKDC Subjective Knee Form), radiographic findings (joint space width and Kellgren-Lawrence grade)
articles.take_home: Transplanted menisci showed greater extrusion than normal menisci on ultrasound scans, particularly in medial transplants, but this extrusion did not relate to how well the knee worked or signs of joint wear on X-rays at 13 years follow-up. This suggests ultrasound extrusion measurements alone are not useful for predicting clinical outcomes after meniscus transplant.

articles.title: Preresection hyperextension is associated with greater initial extension laxity and site-specific reductions in bone resection without substantial joint-line lowering in robot-assisted cruciate-retaining total knee arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Morita Y, Shin J, El-Hassan M, Shichman I, Lewis S, Dundon JM, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing robot-assisted cruciate-retaining total knee replacement
articles.sample_size: 258 knees (149 control, 76 mild hyperextension, 33 greater hyperextension)
articles.outcomes: Intraoperative extension laxity, bone resection amounts, joint-line height, 6-week extension, 1-year KOOS-JR scores, patient acceptable symptom state
articles.take_home: Knees that started surgery with greater backward bending (hyperextension) showed looser extension after surgery and required smaller bone cuts in specific areas. Patients with greater hyperextension were more likely to report poorer symptom control at 1 year, suggesting surgeons should adjust their cutting strategy based on each patient's starting knee position.

articles.title: The biplanar cut in medial closing-wedge distal femoral osteotomy is associated with a four-fold lower rate of lateral hinge fractures at non-inferior coronal correction.
articles.authors: Maione A, Pozzi P, Gallizzi S, Parmigiani MD, Romano S, Menon A, et al.
articles.population: Patients with genu valgum (knock knees) undergoing medial closing-wedge distal femoral osteotomy
articles.sample_size: 82 patients (86 knees): 44 knees monoplanar technique, 42 knees biplanar technique
articles.outcomes: Primary: hip-knee-ankle angle and lateral distal femoral angle correction. Secondary: hinge fracture rate, complications, patient-reported outcomes (pain, function, activity level)
articles.take_home: Using a biplanar cutting technique for knee straightening surgery reduced hinge fractures from 75% to 19% compared to the standard single-cut method, whilst achieving the same degree of correction. Both approaches improved pain and function significantly.

articles.title: Greater eccentric hamstrings to concentric quadriceps strength ratio at 6 months after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction is associated with reduced odds of revision within 2 years.
articles.authors: Hogberg J, Cristiani R, Samuelsson K, Mikkelsen C, Hamrin Senorski E
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study from registry data
articles.population: Patients aged 15 years or older who had primary anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction with hamstring tendon autografts, without other ligament injuries or meniscal resection
articles.outcomes: Association between eccentric hamstrings-to-concentric quadriceps strength ratio at 6 months and revision ACL reconstruction within 2 years; association with single-leg hop symmetry
articles.take_home: Patients with greater hamstring strength relative to quadriceps strength at 6 months after ACL surgery were less likely to need revision surgery within 2 years, but this strength measurement alone is not reliable enough to predict who will need revision surgery. The study suggests this strength ratio may be one useful piece of information when evaluating recovery after ACL surgery.

articles.title: Meniscal and chondral injury patterns in 331 futsal players undergoing anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction: Revision cases are associated with increased chondral pathology.
articles.authors: Barastegui D, Ferre-Aniorte A, Velasco P, Vazquez M, Ayestaran I, Alvarez-Diaz P, et al.
articles.population: Futsal players undergoing ACL reconstruction
articles.outcomes: Prevalence of meniscal tears (51.4%) and chondral lesions (20.5%); revision cases had significantly higher chondral lesion rates (55.9% vs 16.2%)
articles.take_home: Futsal players having knee surgery for ACL injury often have additional cartilage or meniscus damage at the time of surgery. Players having repeat ACL surgery have substantially more cartilage damage, though most damage is early-stage and its long-term importance is not yet clear.

articles.title: Objective arthrometric assessment of sagittal stability after total knee arthroplasty : a prospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Mancino F, Wilson HK, Jain M, Wittauer M, Brockman S, Khorshid O, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Sagittal stability measured by arthrometer, Oxford Knee Score, KOOS, Patient Knee Implant Performance score, EQ-5D-5L questionnaire, and range of motion at 3 and 12 months
articles.take_home: Posterior-stabilised knee implants showed better mechanical stability on testing compared to cruciate-retaining implants, but this did not result in better patient-reported outcomes or functional improvements in the first year after surgery.

articles.title: 2025 International Consensus Meeting Definition of Success for Treatment of Periprosthetic Joint Infection.
articles.authors: Tarabichi S, Verhey JT, Bhandari M, Diaz-Ledezma C, Vaznaisiene D, Bingham JS, et al.
articles.population: Patients with periprosthetic joint infection following total joint arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Treatment success defined as absence of clinical failure after reimplantation, no revision surgery for infection, no suppressive antibiotics beyond one year, and no infection-related death
articles.take_home: An international expert group has agreed on a new standard definition of successful treatment for joint infections after joint replacement surgery, aiming to make research findings more consistent and comparable across hospitals. Previously, reported success rates varied widely from 54% to 89% because different studies used different definitions.

articles.title: Total Hip Arthroplasty for Femoral Neck Fracture Has Distinct Complication and Revision Risks Compared with Osteoarthritis Through 15 Years.
articles.authors: Boutany M, Abdelnour D, Elnaggar A, Vaidya R, Little B, Darwiche H
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using national database with propensity score matching
articles.population: Patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty for femoral neck fracture compared with osteoarthritis
articles.outcomes: Mortality, periprosthetic fracture, periprosthetic joint infection, dislocation, revision surgery, and mechanical loosening at 90 days and 15 years
articles.take_home: Patients having hip replacement for a broken femur neck have higher risks of complications than those having it for arthritis, including more infections, fractures around the implant, dislocations and revision surgery lasting up to 15 years. The risks were particularly high in the first 90 days after surgery.

articles.title: Can We Target the Microbiome to Improve Outcomes in Osteoarthritis and Arthroplasty?
articles.authors: Pourbozorg G, Heckmann ND, Mont MA, Lieberman JR, Parvizi J
articles.population: People with osteoarthritis and those undergoing joint replacement surgery
articles.outcomes: Osteoarthritis progression, joint inflammation, cartilage degeneration, periprosthetic joint infection risk, immune response
articles.take_home: Research suggests that gut bacteria may influence both osteoarthritis and the risk of infection after joint replacement surgery, and that changing diet, taking probiotics, or increasing physical activity might help. However, most evidence is from laboratory studies rather than patient trials, so more research in people is needed before these approaches can be recommended routinely.

articles.title: Femoral Neck Morphology: A Computed-Tomography-Based Anatomic Framework Informs Medial Collar Design for Contemporary Collared Cementless Femoral Stems.
articles.authors: Kelly JJ, Helgeson EE, Alshaibi RR, Rhodes NG, Pagnano MW, Hevesi M
articles.study_type: Retrospective observational study using computed tomography imaging
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Femoral neck cortical thickness measurements at the bone-cutting level and adjacent levels; optimal medial collar length for cementless femoral stems
articles.take_home: The thickest bone support in the femoral neck is found in the medial and back-medial areas, increasing towards the direction of the planned cut. A collar length of 5.3 millimetres best matches the bone thickness at the cutting level for the implants studied.

articles.title: Cefazolin Administration in Patients Who Have Severe Penicillin Allergy Undergoing Total Joint Arthroplasty: A Prospective Observational Study.
articles.authors: Samineni AV, Cruz-Ossa N, Reddy GB, McNamara CA, Hernandez VH, D'Apuzzo MR
articles.population: Patients with documented severe penicillin allergy undergoing total hip or knee replacement
articles.outcomes: Primary: allergic reactions (anaphylaxis, rash) within six hours of surgery. Secondary: surgical site infection and periprosthetic joint infection.
articles.take_home: No allergic reactions occurred in 51 patients with reported severe penicillin allergy who received cefazolin during joint replacement surgery. The researchers suggest cefazolin may be safer in these patients than currently assumed, but larger studies are needed to confirm this finding.

articles.title: The Impact of Tourniquet Duration on Postoperative Opioid Use and Recovery After Total Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Weinblatt AI, Lan R, Oettl FC, Ondeck NT, Gonzalez AG, Lyman S, et al.
articles.population: Adults undergoing primary unilateral total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Postoperative opioid use (morphine milligram equivalents), time to physiotherapy clearance, manipulation under anaesthesia within 120 days, and patient-reported knee function at six weeks
articles.take_home: Using a tourniquet for only part of the operation was linked to lower opioid use over 90 days compared to no tourniquet, whilst using it for the whole operation increased opioid use and delayed physiotherapy clearance. Partial tourniquet use may offer a better balance of benefits and risks.

articles.title: Smaller Lateral Gap Than the Medial Gap in Deep-Flexion was Associated with Lower Patient Satisfaction in Robotic-Assisted Restricted Kinematically Aligned Cruciate-Retaining Total Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Nakamura Y, Ogawa H, Ota Y, Onishi K, Akiyama H
articles.population: Patients undergoing robotic-assisted restricted kinematically aligned cruciate-retaining total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Knee Society Score satisfaction, WOMAC pain score, Forgotten Joint Score-12, radiographic parameters, intraoperative component gaps
articles.take_home: Knees where the gap between the implant surfaces was smaller on the outer side than the inner side during deep bending had lower patient satisfaction and more pain than knees with a larger outer gap. Surgeons may need to adjust how they position the implant to achieve better gap balance during knee bending.

articles.title: Undervaluing Revision: Reimbursement Disparities in Primary, Conversion, and Revision Total Knee and Hip Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Denyer S, Tseng J, D'Ambrose N, Benson M, Schmitt D, Brown N
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary, conversion, and revision total knee and hip arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Operative time, complications, readmission, reoperation, mortality, and reimbursement per operative minute
articles.take_home: Revision knee and hip replacements take significantly longer and have much higher complication rates than primary surgery, but surgeons are paid less per minute for doing them. The study found that real-term reimbursement for joint replacement surgery has fallen by 35 to 45% since 2006 even after accounting for inflation.

articles.title: Clinical outcome of a modern patellofemoral arthroplasty prosthesis into the second decade - a cohort study with minimum 10-year follow-up.
articles.authors: Tsikopoulos K, White P, Musawi HA, Newman J, Porteous A, Robinson J, et al.
articles.population: Patients who received a modern patellofemoral joint arthroplasty (PFA) prosthesis
articles.sample_size: 161 replacements with mean follow-up of 13.8 years
articles.outcomes: Implant survivorship, revision rates, Oxford Knee Score, complications and mortality
articles.take_home: This modern patellofemoral joint replacement had good long-term survival, with 81% of implants still working at 10 years and 75% at 20 years. Patients had significantly better knee function scores up to 5 years after surgery, though some implants needed revision, most commonly due to worsening osteoarthritis.

articles.title: Technology Assistance and Fixed-Bearing Design Were Associated with Higher Revision-Free Survival at 15 Years After UKA: A Cohort Study of 2,234 Consecutive Knees.
articles.authors: Tsukamoto I, MacInnis BR, Grimm JA, Bedard NA, Sierra RJ, Pagnano MW, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary unicompartmental knee arthroplasty for isolated compartment osteoarthritis
articles.outcomes: Revision-free survivorship at 10 and 15 years, risk factors for revision, Knee Society Score clinical outcomes
articles.take_home: Unicompartmental knee replacement showed good long-term durability with 92% of implants surviving at 10 years and 85% at 15 years. Using fixed-bearing implants and technology assistance during surgery were associated with lower revision rates.

articles.title: Global Trends in Unicompartmental Knee Arthroplasty: A Multi-Registry Analysis of Usage and Implant Choices.
articles.authors: Gravemaker DS, Jensen CB, Troelsen A, Zuiderbaan HA
articles.population: Patients undergoing knee arthroplasty in nine countries
articles.sample_size: National knee arthroplasty registry data from 2014 to 2024
articles.outcomes: Usage rates of unicompartmental knee arthroplasty, fixation methods, implant design choices, and compartment distribution
articles.take_home: Unicompartmental knee arthroplasty is underused globally, ranging from 3.5% to 36.6% of knee replacements across countries, despite evidence that up to 50% of patients could be suitable for this bone-preserving procedure. Usage is increasing overall but varies significantly between countries, and most procedures use cemented fixation and target the medial compartment.

articles.title: Knee flexion influences MRI-based static tibiofemoral rotation after ACL injury and reconstruction.
articles.authors: Ackermann J, Jones M, Ball SV, Kabeer AS, Bamania P, Watura C, et al.
articles.population: Professional soccer players with ACL injury and after ACL reconstruction
articles.outcomes: Static tibiofemoral rotation measured on MRI, posterior tibial slope asymmetry, knee flexion angle
articles.take_home: How much the knee is bent during an MRI scan affects measurements of knee rotation after ACL injury, with differences in knee bend of 10-20 degrees potentially creating false rotation differences of 1.5-3 degrees. Researchers recommend standardising knee bend angle when using MRI to measure rotation for research purposes.

articles.title: Femoral Neck System for young and middle-aged adult femoral neck fractures: a trade-off between reduced lateral irritation and increased neck shortening.
articles.authors: Quanwei B, Huanyu S, Xiaoyong M, Jing Y, Jiangyuan L, Yamei Z, et al.
articles.population: Young and middle-aged adults with femoral neck fractures
articles.sample_size: 55 patients (28 in Femoral Neck System group, 27 in cannulated screws group)
articles.outcomes: Time to full weight-bearing, Hip Harris Score and EQ-5D-5L score at 6 and 12 months, femoral neck shortening at 12 months, complication rates
articles.take_home: The Femoral Neck System allowed patients to bear weight faster (4 weeks versus 6 weeks) and caused no lateral thigh pain, but cost more money and led to greater shortening of the femoral neck. Both treatments produced similar functional results and overall complication rates over 12 months.

articles.title: Institutional Case Volume as a Determinant of the Operative Efficiency in Robotic-Assisted Total Hip Arthroplasty: Analysis of the American Joint Replacement Registry.
articles.authors: Katchis CS, Haikal ER, Zaniletti I, Ang BK, Lafage V, Slover JD
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary elective robotic-assisted total hip arthroplasty in US institutions
articles.sample_size: 46,805 cases across 305 institutions between January 2017 and December 2024
articles.outcomes: Operative time and achievement of efficiency threshold (median operative time of 90 minutes or less), stratified by institutional surgical volume
articles.take_home: Hospitals that perform more robotic hip replacements achieve faster and more consistent surgery times. High-volume centres needed about 300 procedures to reach efficient surgery times of 90 minutes or less, whilst low-volume centres struggled to reach this benchmark even with practice.

articles.title: Bayesian Statistics for Arthroplasty Surgeons: Moving Beyond Simple "Yes or No" P-Values to Probabilistic Clinical Decision-Making.
articles.authors: Hoskins W, Gusho C, Parola R, Slobogean G, O'Hara N
articles.population: Arthroplasty surgeons and researchers
articles.outcomes: Understanding of Bayesian statistical principles and their application to hip and knee arthroplasty research
articles.take_home: Bayesian statistics offer an alternative approach to traditional P-value methods that may better reflect real-world clinical reasoning by incorporating prior knowledge and providing probabilistic statements rather than simple yes-or-no conclusions. Whilst most Bayesian analysis in orthopaedics currently comes from reanalysing existing studies, the use of Bayesian methods in arthroplasty research is growing.

articles.title: Kinematic alignment reduces tibial internal rotation and maintains a larger retropatellar contact area than mechanical alignment in early flexion in valgus knees.
articles.authors: Simon JM, Simon F, Siedow TM, Thorwachter C, Traxler H, Bauer L, et al.
articles.study_type: Laboratory experimental study using cadaveric specimens
articles.population: Valgus knees (with outward deviation)
articles.outcomes: Tibial rotation, patellar contact area, patellar tilt, dynamic valgus deviation, quadriceps force during knee flexion
articles.take_home: In valgus knees, kinematic alignment (KA) reduced excessive inward rotation of the tibia and maintained a larger contact area between the kneecap and thighbone compared to mechanical alignment, particularly in early bending. However, neither technique fully matched how a native knee moves, and the study could not definitively show which approach is superior in real patients.

articles.title: Gracilis tendon harvest for ACL reconstruction impairs gracilis muscle volume recovery and may adversely affect adjacent thigh musculature. MRI-based outcomes from a subgroup of patients enroled in the DOSTAR randomized controlled trial.
articles.authors: Davies PSE, Banziger C, Lawless AM, O'Brien SS, Ebert JR, Edwards PK, et al.
articles.study_type: Subgroup analysis of a prospective randomised controlled trial
articles.population: Patients undergoing anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction
articles.sample_size: 38 patients with MRI scans at 6 and 12 months
articles.outcomes: Thigh muscle volume changes measured by MRI at 6 and 12 months post-operatively, comparing gracilis and adductor longus muscles between single tendon (semitendinosus) and dual tendon (semitendinosus and gracilis) graft groups
articles.take_home: Using the gracilis tendon for ACL reconstruction resulted in poorer recovery of the gracilis muscle and the adjacent adductor longus muscle compared to using only the semitendinosus tendon. This suggests that single tendon grafts may be preferable for preserving thigh muscle function after ACL surgery.

articles.title: The presence of cement pockets on the tibial component undersurface is associated with reduced revision for aseptic tibial loosening-A single-centre study of 11,594 total knee arthroplasties.
articles.authors: Firth AM, Remtulla M, Vorasatit L, Nightingale J, Berber R, Matar HE, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary cemented total knee arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 11,594 total knee arthroplasties (8,591 fixed bearing; 3,003 mobile bearing)
articles.outcomes: Revision for aseptic tibial loosening and all-cause revision
articles.take_home: Tibial implants with cement pockets (recessed areas at the implant-cement interface) significantly reduced the need for revision surgery due to aseptic loosening, particularly for fixed bearing designs. This effect was not seen with mobile bearing implants.

articles.title: No significant differences in complication and graft failure rates by type of surgery or osteotomy level after slope-reducing osteotomy with ACL reconstruction: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Pineda T, Pena J, Arriagada G, Ugarte J, Olivieri R, Ollivier M
articles.population: Adults undergoing anterior closing wedge high tibial osteotomy combined with ACL reconstruction
articles.outcomes: ACL graft failure rates, complication rates including symptomatic hardware, reintervention rates, delayed union or non-union, deep infections, vascular or thromboembolic events, and postoperative recurvatum
articles.take_home: This surgery combining knee realignment with ACL reconstruction appears safe with low rates of graft failure and major complications across different surgical approaches and timing. However, the evidence quality is very low, so we cannot be certain which surgical method works best or whether combining both procedures offers real benefits over ACL reconstruction alone.

articles.title: Male-female differences in unilateral jump-landing energetics are concentrated in propulsion-phase work generation across self-paced and ball-interception tasks in competitive soccer players.
articles.authors: AminiAghdam S, Woergoetter S, Scharbert J, Baumert P, Fink C
articles.population: Competitive soccer players
articles.sample_size: 45 players (22 males aged 18.4 +/- 2.1 years; 23 females aged 20.1 +/- 3.5 years)
articles.outcomes: Jump height, reactive strength index, propulsion-phase work generation, braking and landing phase work absorption, and joint-specific contributions during single-leg countermovement jumps and soccer-relevant jump-heading-landing tasks
articles.take_home: Male players in this study showed greater jump height and stronger knee power during the push-off phase of jumping compared to female players, whilst female players relied more on ankle power. The ability to generate knee power during push-off was linked to jumping higher, particularly during soccer-specific jumping tasks.

articles.title: Individualised total knee arthroplasty results in low reintervention rates for stiffness and instability in 1000 consecutive knees, regardless of intraoperative bone recuts or polyethylene thickness.
articles.authors: Schmidt A, Sappey-Marinier E, Alajji M, Ferrini A, Ait-Si-Selmi T, Bonnin M
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty using a CT-based individualised system
articles.outcomes: Revision total knee arthroplasty rates, reintervention rates for stiffness and instability, revision-free and reoperation-free survival at 1 and 5 years
articles.take_home: Individualised total knee replacement had low rates of revision (1.2%) and reintervention for stiffness or instability (2.9%) over an average of 4.2 years. Adjustments made during surgery, such as bone recuts, did not increase the risk of needing further surgery.

articles.title: The restricted 4D inverse kinematic alignment workflow: A patient-specific approach integrating both bony and laxity phenotypes for total knee arthroplasty planning.
articles.authors: Graichen H, Hirschmann MT, Avram GM, Vandekerckhove PJ, Winnock de Grave P, Indelli PF, et al.
articles.population: Knees undergoing total knee arthroplasty planning
articles.outcomes: Achievement of target laxity phenotype, maintenance of native alignment angles, posterior condylar offset measurements, flexion and extension gap balancing
articles.take_home: A new personalised planning technique for knee replacement that considers both bone shape and ligament laxity can achieve the desired laxity goals in nearly all cases, but often requires greater adjustments to the back of the thighbone than standard techniques.

articles.title: Effect of Joint Loadings, Ligament Tensions, and Total Knee Designs on Kinematics During Flexion.
articles.authors: Parody N, Rozell JC, Walker PS
articles.population: Four different non-cruciate total knee arthroplasty designs tested in a crouching machine
articles.sample_size: Four TKA designs with three collateral ligament tension conditions each
articles.outcomes: Femoral and tibial motion during knee flexion (12 to 130 degrees) under low and high load conditions, measuring medial and lateral displacements and axial rotation
articles.take_home: Most knee replacement designs moved differently when tested under light surgical conditions compared to real functional loading, but one design (replica intercondylar) behaved similarly in both situations. The replica intercondylar design achieved consistent motion mainly through its shaped bearing surfaces rather than relying heavily on ligament tension.

articles.title: Inflammatory Markers Following Robotic-Assisted Versus Manual Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Ade-Conde M, Son H, Lanting BA, Howard JL, Khalik HA
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty, mean age 67 years, 66% women, mean BMI 28.4
articles.outcomes: Postoperative inflammatory markers including C-reactive protein, white blood cell count, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, and operative time
articles.take_home: Robotic-assisted knee replacement was associated with slightly lower inflammation markers in the first three days after surgery compared with manual surgery, but these differences had disappeared by one month. Robotic surgery took about 11 minutes longer.

articles.title: Trends in Single versus Multiple Component Revision for Total Knee Arthroplasty Instability and Subsequent Revision-Free Survival: A Large Retrospective Analysis.
articles.authors: Magaldi RJ, Smith H, Ong W, Post ZD, Ponzio D, Ong A
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort analysis using national database
articles.population: Patients undergoing revision knee replacement for instability between 2010 and 2024
articles.outcomes: Five-year revision-free survival rates: 85.4% for single-component revision versus 86.7% for multiple-component revision
articles.take_home: Single-component knee revision surgery (replacing just one part) has become increasingly popular and appears to work as well as replacing multiple parts, with similar rates of needing further surgery within five years.

articles.title: Declining Complications After Primary Total Knee Arthroplasty Over 16 Years.
articles.authors: Wajahath M, Saad J, Elmenini H, Al Jamal M, Saleh KJ, Vaidya R
articles.study_type: Observational cohort study using national database
articles.population: Adults undergoing primary total knee replacement for knee osteoarthritis
articles.outcomes: 90-day outcomes: periprosthetic joint infection, deep vein thrombosis, transfusion, sepsis and others. 2-year outcomes: revision surgery, infection, aseptic loosening, mechanical complications, implant-related complications, manipulation under anaesthesia and periprosthetic fracture
articles.take_home: Complications after primary knee replacement have significantly declined between 2008 and 2023, with infections, blood clots and need for transfusion all becoming less common despite more operations being performed and patients being older. Most complications improved over this 16-year period, providing up-to-date benchmarks for what to expect.

articles.title: A Randomized Controlled Trial Examining the Effects of Extended Oral Tranexamic Acid on Postoperative Pain and Range of Motion Following Total Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Grosso MJ, Panek G, Weinz C, Hahn AK, Bauer JA
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Visual analogue scale pain scores, range of motion, opioid consumption, and ambulation status at multiple timepoints up to 12 weeks postoperatively
articles.take_home: Extended oral tranexamic acid taken for three days after knee replacement surgery did not reduce pain, improve movement, reduce opioid use, or improve walking ability compared with placebo. The researchers concluded this treatment approach may not be worth using routinely in knee replacement surgery.

articles.title: Survivorship of Fixed-Bearing Lateral Unicompartmental Knee Arthroplasty: Minimum 10-Year Follow-up of a Single-Center Cohort.
articles.authors: Jager T, Winnock de Grave P, Ryckaert A, Tampere T, Luyckx T
articles.population: Patients who underwent fixed-bearing lateral unicompartmental knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Revision-free survivorship at 5, 10 and 15 years; reasons for revision
articles.take_home: Fixed-bearing lateral knee replacements had a 90.6% survival rate at 10 and 15 years, with most failures happening in the first five years after surgery, usually due to arthritis developing in other parts of the knee.

articles.title: Increased risk of infection and reoperation following total knee arthroplasty in patients under 40.
articles.authors: Daley A, Yarden J, Diaz-Coto S, Moschetti W
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using electronic health records
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty, stratified by age (under 40 versus over 65 years)
articles.outcomes: Infection, superficial wound dehiscence, readmission and need for further surgery on the same knee, measured at 90 days and 1 year after surgery
articles.take_home: Younger patients under 40 having knee replacement surgery face higher risks of infection and needing another operation compared to patients over 65, even after accounting for smoking and other health conditions. This increased risk was particularly pronounced in patients who needed surgery for multiple reasons.

articles.title: Short-term outcomes of robotic-assisted direct anterior THA in patients with generalised ligamentous laxity: a propensity-matched study.
articles.authors: Quesada-Jimenez R, Reyes-Cordova A, Patel DH, Kuhns BD, Kahana-Rojkind AH, Domb BG
articles.population: Patients with generalised ligamentous laxity undergoing robotic-assisted direct anterior total hip arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 126 patients (42 with generalised ligamentous laxity, 84 controls)
articles.outcomes: Patient-reported outcome measures (Harris Hip Score, HOOS-JR, Forgotten Joint Score, pain scores), satisfaction, revision rates, dislocation rates
articles.take_home: Patients with generalised ligamentous laxity who had robotic-assisted hip replacement through the direct anterior approach achieved similar improvements and satisfaction compared to those without ligamentous laxity, with no dislocations in either group at 2-year follow-up. Revision rates were very low and similar between groups.
